sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order -- location order below, which is page order and, within a page, the two-column reading order (left column top-to-bottom, then right column, each table or figure taken at the point its float is printed in that column), row-major within a table and left-to-right across that row's own-result columns only. That gives a population of 1..170. SimSiam is a short paper that is almost entirely its own ablations, so ownership is unusually simple: all but one table contains only the authors' own runs, and the two places a prior method's number could be quoted are settled by explicit statements rather than by inference. Table 4's caption says 'All competitors are from our reproduction, and "+" denotes improved reproduction vs. original papers', so all 20 of its accuracy cells are own results, the four named prior methods included -- a reproduction the authors ran is an own result because that number was produced by this artifact. Table C.1 is the one table with a genuine baseline row: its 'origin' row is explicitly the original papers' published figures (8 printed numbers plus one '-') and is excluded, while its 'repro.' row (7 printed numbers plus two '-') is own. In Table 5, Sec. 6.1 states 'We use the public codebase from MoCo [17] for all entries, and search the fine-tuning learning rate for each individual method', so all 96 cells of its 8 rows x 12 columns are counted own; the two rows above the rule ('scratch', printed in grey, and 'ImageNet supervised') are the least certain reading in the paper, and a cell drawn from either is labelled confident:false rather than silently counted (frame_index 70 is one such draw). Non-numeric entries are not cells: Table 3d's 'unstable', the SwAV ablation's 'NaN' and the four '-' entries in Table C.1 have no value to transcribe. A value printed as mean+/-std contributes its point value only (Figure 2's '67.7+/-0.1' is one cell at 67.7). Architecture and optimisation settings are hyperparameters throughout and are excluded: Table 2's batch-size header row, Table 4's 'batch size' column and its epoch headers, Table 3's BN checkmark columns, Table C.1's 'epoch' row, the output dimension d in Appendix B, and every setting in Sec. 3's 'Baseline settings' and in Appendix A. A prose delta is counted when no absolute is printed beside it in the same passage -- Sec. 4.3's 'a drop of 0.8% or 2.0% in accuracy' (2 cells; the corresponding absolutes are in Table 2, a different location), Appendix A's '~1% lower accuracy' for the alternative SGD linear-evaluation optimizer, and Appendix D's 'slightly better by 0.7%' (its absolutes are in Figure D.1's embedded table, a separate location) -- while a prose restatement of a table value in a new location is counted as its own printed instance, as in Sec. 4.1's 67.7%/0.1% and Sec. 4.4's 34.6%/67.4%/68.1%. Two prose numbers that look like results are excluded as theory rather than measurement: the loss floor of -1 ('its minimum possible value is -1', Sec. 3, reached in Sec. 4.1) and the std 1/sqrt(d) of a zero-mean isotropic Gaussian; footnote 4's parenthetical '(0.1%)' is likewise excluded as a statement of ImageNet chance level rather than a second measurement. The two numbers quoted from BYOL in Sec. 2 (0.3% accuracy, and footnote 2's 66.9%) are citation baselines and excluded, as is the whole 'origin' row of Table C.1. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 171), 15) drew {1, 2, 13, 14, 25, 29, 70, 83, 91, 99, 107, 108, 122, 148, 153}; each label below records its draw as frame_index.
